cases.statement:
Batch transfers leave partial balance changes when a later transfer is rejected. Repair evaluate(balances, transfers) and the transfer helper. Transfers have source, target and amount; require existing accounts, a positive integer amount, and sufficient funds. Boolean amounts are invalid. Apply the entire batch atomically or return the original balances unchanged. Transfers to the same account are permitted when funded and have no net effect. Do not mutate either input, even on success.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

The batch exporter drops a partial final batch. Repair evaluate(items, size) to return consecutive batches, retaining all items and their order. Size is a positive integer. Do not pad or modify the input.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

Import rows containing escaped separators are split incorrectly. Repair evaluate(line) to split on unescaped vertical bars. Backslash escapes the next character, including a separator or another backslash; a final unmatched backslash is literal. Retain empty fields and do not trim whitespace.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

A credentials panel still considers entries usable at their expiration instant. Repair evaluate(now, expiresAt, enabled). Both times are finite numeric clock ticks. An entry is usable only while enabled and strictly before expiration.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

The scheduling badge reports a clash when appointments only touch. Repair Evaluate(a, b), where each argument is an ordered half-open integer interval. Report overlap only if the intersection has positive width; empty intervals never overlap.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

Recovery replays duplicate journal records and can move a record backwards in revision. Repair Evaluate(events) and the revision policy. Each Event has ID, Key, Revision, Value and Deleted. Process each event ID only once, even when a later duplicate changes its contents. For a key, retain only a strictly newer revision; equal revisions keep the earlier event. Deletions retain revision history but are omitted from the returned live value map. Inputs remain unchanged.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

The export deduplicator keeps whichever record arrived last, ignoring record revisions. Repair evaluate(records) to retain the highest revision for each id, keep the earlier record on a revision tie, and return records in first-seen id order. Records have id, revision, and value. Leave inputs untouched.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

The activity list sometimes returns too many rows on later pages. Repair evaluate(items, offset, limit) so pagination returns at most limit rows starting at the nonnegative offset. Inputs are arrays and nonnegative integers. Preserve item order and leave the input unchanged.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

The log formatter strips unrelated letters from both ends of messages. Repair evaluate(text, prefix) to remove one exact prefix only when it occurs at the beginning. An empty prefix leaves the message unchanged. Keep all remaining whitespace and suffixes.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

Search links lose repeated filters and blank selections. Repair evaluate(query) to return a plain object mapping every decoded key to all its decoded values in encounter order. Accept a query with or without the leading question mark. Follow URLSearchParams decoding, including form-style spaces; do not lose special object property names.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

Retries can sleep beyond the configured cap and the first retry waits too long. Repair evaluate(base, attempt, cap, remaining): attempt is a nonnegative retry index, beginning with the first retry. Exponential delay starts at base and doubles per subsequent attempt, bounded by both cap and remaining. All other inputs are finite nonnegative numbers. Large attempts must stay bounded.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

The text compressor drops the last run and counts bytes instead of characters. Repair Evaluate(text) to return consecutive runs as Run structs containing a rune and its count, in encounter order. Empty input yields an allocated empty slice. Adjacent equal runes belong to the same run.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

The sorted stream merger drops tails and shared values. Repair Evaluate(left, right) to merge sorted integer slices into a sorted result retaining every occurrence. Do not modify or alias either input. Return an allocated empty slice when both inputs are empty.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

Warehouse availability drifts after duplicate reservation deliveries and releases. Repair evaluate(initial, events), using the existing reducer and inventory module. Events reserve a positive quantity under a unique id or release that id. Accept a reservation only if enough stock remains; duplicate live ids and unknown releases do nothing. A release restores exactly its accepted quantity and allows reuse of the id. Other event kinds are ignored. Return available stock after all events; rejected reservations must leave no record.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.

The batch scheduler underallocates workers when work does not divide evenly. Repair Evaluate(items, capacity) to return the smallest worker count that can process all items without exceeding per-worker capacity. Items are nonnegative, capacity is positive, and both fit in int. Avoid overflowing intermediate arithmetic.

Keep the existing public entry point. Use only the standard library.
